title: Building Through Market Uncertainty
excerpt: A practical archive note on maintaining clarity through changing construction conditions.
body:
Costs move, availability shifts and timelines stretch. None of that has to derail a project, provided the decisions stay legible and the scope stays clear.

This archive note sets out how we hold a steady direction through changing construction conditions: keeping the brief visible, testing decisions against the realities of making, and appointing the right specialist input when the project needs it rather than all at once. Clarity, not speed, is what protects a build when the market is unsettled.

title: Construction Cost per Square Foot in Sri Lanka: 2026 Guide and Calculator
excerpt: Use Excello's construction cost calculator to create an early planning estimate, then understand how site conditions, design, finishes and scope influence the final building budget.
body:
A cost per square foot is a useful starting point, not an answer. It gives you an early planning estimate you can reason with, before drawings and appointments turn a budget into a real number.

This guide walks through how to build that early estimate, then explains how site conditions, design decisions, finishes and scope move the figure up or down. The aim is a budget you understand, so that later conversations about materials and programme are about choices, not surprises.

title: Aathavan Residential Project Launched
excerpt: An archive update covering the launch of Aathavan Apartments in Dehiwala.
body:
Aathavan Apartments brings together 44 residences at No. 6 Carron Place, Dehiwala, with a mix of two- and three-bedroom homes, selected units with maid's quarters, rooftop amenities, solar infrastructure and parking.

This update marks the launch of the project and Excello's role across development, architectural coordination, interior direction and build-stage collaboration. The aim is a calm, durable and well-resolved home environment where planning, material choices and long-term usability work together.

title: How to Design a Spacious House on a Small Plot in Sri Lanka
excerpt: Learn how efficient planning, courtyards, vertical space, storage and climate-responsive design can create a comfortable home on a small Sri Lankan plot.
body:
A small plot is a constraint, not a compromise. With efficient planning it can hold a home that feels generous, private and light.

This note looks at the moves that make a compact house work: courtyards and voids that borrow light and air, vertical space used well, storage designed in rather than added on, and a climate-responsive section that keeps interiors cool. The result is a comfortable home that makes the most of every square foot of a Sri Lankan plot.

title: Luxury Living: Creating a High-End Look on a Budget
excerpt: An architect guide to thoughtful material, lighting and spatial decisions within a defined budget.
body:
A high-end look is not the same as a high budget. It comes from proportion, restraint and a few well-placed decisions, not from spending everywhere.

This architect's guide covers where thoughtful choices earn the most: honest materials used simply, lighting that shapes a room after dark, and spatial decisions that give everyday moments a sense of calm. Spend on the things people touch and stand in, and let restraint do the rest.

title: Design and Build vs Architect and Contractor: Which Approach Is Right for Your Home?
excerpt: Compare design-and-build with the traditional architect-and-contractor method, including responsibilities, cost control, design quality and project risks.
body:
The route you choose to build shapes how decisions are made, who is accountable and where the risk sits. Neither approach is automatically better; they suit different briefs.

This note compares design-and-build with the traditional architect-and-contractor method across the things that matter: responsibilities and single-point accountability, cost control, design quality, and where the project risk lands. Read alongside your brief and site, it should make the right first step clearer.
